title: Agan-Unitsi's Search for the Uktena
subtitle: A dangerous hunt for the serpent's talisman

learningObjectives.text: Where does Agan-Unitsi finally find the Uktena?
How does he keep the serpent's poison from reaching him?

search.author: James Mooney
search.excerpt: Other places he tried, going always southward, and at last on Gahû'ti mountain he found the Uktena asleep.
search.note: Verbatim English text from Mooney's 1902 collection. Keep the specific numbered story and its East Cherokee/recorded-source context attached.

hunt.author: James Mooney
hunt.excerpt: The Uktena was still asleep, and, putting an arrow to his bow, Âgan-uni'tsi shot and sent the arrow through its heart, which was under the seventh spot from the serpent's head. The great snake raised his head, with the diamond in front flashing fire, and came straight at his enemy, but the magician, turning quickly, ran at full speed down the mountain, cleared the circle of fire and the trench at one bound, and lay down on the ground inside. The Uktena tried to follow, but the arrow was through his heart, and in another moment he rolled over in his death struggle, spitting poison over all the mountain side. But the poison drops could not pass the circle of fire, but only hissed and sputtered in the blaze, and the magician on the inside was untouched except by one small drop
hunt.note: Verbatim English text from Mooney's 1902 collection. Keep the specific numbered story and its East Cherokee/recorded-source context attached.

crystal.author: James Mooney
crystal.excerpt: The blazing diamond is called Ulûñsû'ti, "Transparent," and he who can win it may become the greatest wonder worker of the tribe, but it is worth a man's life to attempt it

narrativeBlocks.title: A promise to find the Uktena
narrativeBlocks.body: Mooney's story says Agan-Unitsi is captured in war and promises to find the dangerous Uktena and its bright talisman.

narrativeBlocks.title: The search reaches Gahû'ti
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Mooney's English record (whitespace normalized): “Other places he tried, going always southward, and at last on Gahû'ti mountain he found the Uktena asleep.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A plan rather than a direct attack
narrativeBlocks.body: Agan-Unitsi makes a circle of pine cones, a trench, and fire before shooting the sleeping serpent beneath the seventh spot.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not turn this into a safety guide
narrativeBlocks.body: This is a recorded Cherokee narrative about a dangerous being and a powerful object. It is not advice for approaching wildlife or a claim about present-day Cherokee practice.

narrativeBlocks.title: The prize carries danger
narrativeBlocks.body: The narrative pairs the Uktena's crystal with danger to the hunter and his family; its power is not presented as consequence-free.
